This unit is versatile enough for various exercises, including low rows, pull-ups, chin-ups, squats, bench presses, powerlifting, CrossFit, and Olympic lifting.

The Fitness Reality Squat Rack Power Cage has an official weight capacity of 800 pounds. This unit can help anyone hit their goals, from beginners to elite powerlifters.

It has been revealed that like all good squat racks, the Fitness Reality Squat Rack Power Cage has solid steel safety arms rather than hollow tubes. It features two rear stability bars. Thanks to 19 adjustable height levels, you can use the unit for various exercises besides squats, including pull-ups, chin-ups, bench presses, and overhead presses. And it’s $299, the most affordable option on our list.

Industry observers note that it has a multi-grip pull-up bar and two 23-inch safety bars with chrome locks. While it doesn’t come with J-hooks, dip bars, or plate storage attachments, one-inch holes allow you to use this equipment with standard-sized attachments.

According to recent reports, A power rack—or power cage—has four uprights designed to serve as a base for powerlifting, Olympic lifting, and other strength training. They are commonly used with a barbell but may have optional attachments for non-barbell exercises using cables or body weight. A full power rack allows athletes to lift inside or outside the cage. Half racks have two uprights, so athletes must lift outside the rack because there is less depth.

Research links strength training, including weightlifting, to long-term health benefits like reducing disease.

It has been revealed that A power rack provides equipment, like safety bars, to help you lift heavy weights safely without a spotter. Some power racks come with add-on attachments, such as pull-up bars and dip bars, to help you get a well-rounded workout. Additionally, most power racks are compatible with accessories you can buy for an extra price to customize your workout for your needs.

Exercisers use a power rack for strength training, Olympic lifting, and powerlifting. Additional attachments, such as a dip station or pull-up bar, allow you to use it for bodyweight exercises. Some have pulley systems for other resistance exercises.

Industry observers note that correctly using a power rack can successfully enhance strength training. “It’s all about consistency,” Sevcik notes. “Make sure you have some kind of progressive overload built into your programming.”.

Recent findings suggest that power racks provide a safe lifting experience, which is of utmost importance, especially if you plan on training alone. The safety straps, pins, or arms—also called safeties—are a critical safety feature. “One of my biggest pet peeves is when I see people who don’t know how to set the safety arms the right way and have the pins set way too low,” Sevcik notes. “The purpose of those safety arms is to give you a safe way to bail out of a lift. Otherwise, you’re just using a power rack as a substantial immobile squat stand.”.

According to recent reports, so, what is the correct way to set up the safety arms? “To set them up for squats, put the unloaded bar on your back and squat down to the deepest position you can get yourself into,” Sevcik indicates. “The safety bars should be about an inch and a half or one notch lower than your bottom position, so if you ever fail on a squat, all you do is sit your butt down to the very bottom.”.

It has been revealed that many come with safety arms, pins, or nylon straps, but some budget options may require purchasing them separately. If you’re new to using a power rack, we recommend asking a fitness professional for guidance on different exercises and safety.

Before purchasing, measure your space and look at the rack’s total footprint. While measuring the floor and comparing it to the base is essential, ceiling height is another crucial factor. You may need a shorter option if you use your rack in a basement or a room with low ceilings.

According to recent reports, you can retract and store a folding power rack if you’re limited in space or need room for other activities. It’s a good idea to consider your height and weight when looking at the dimensions, especially if you plan to use the pull-up bar or other attachments. You may want to leave space on each side for accessories so you can attach them on the sides if necessary. We recommend you keep the space around the rack clear of obstructions, particularly in front, so you can safely complete your lifts or bailout.

Recent findings suggest that power racks come in a variety of styles, colors, and materials. Some construction and style factors to consider include:.

The power racks on this list have capacities ranging from 700 pounds to 1,100 pounds. The lower and middle weight range will likely work for you if you are a beginner or intermediate exerciser. If you are an advanced athlete, you may want to opt for a power rack with a high weight capacity and heavy-duty steel. Attachments such as safety arms, J-hooks, or pull-up bars have varying weight limits. Always stay within the recommended weight range for your safety.

How much you’re willing to spend depends on your budget and training style. Many racks on this list include a basic setup, with the option to add accessories as needed, which cuts the cost. Other racks come fully loaded with accessories, so they are incredibly versatile. However, these options cost more, so it is crucial to consider the features and whether or not they are helpful for your workout style and goals. The racks on this list range from around $299 to $965, and many brands offer free shipping.

It has been revealed that power racks come in various styles and features. The following sections break down Sevcik’s power rack must-haves.

Sevcik says to look for thick, heavy-duty steel such as 11-gauge. “A rack made out of thicker steel creates more leverage on the uprights. Especially when you add those attachments.”.

“I think a significant must-have a lot of people overlook is to make sure your J-cups, or J-hooks, have some coating on them to preserve the knurling on your bar,” Sevcik notes. “If you’re doing a bench press or deadlift, [knurling] is no big deal, but if you’re an Olympic weightlifter, that’s where my snatch grip is holding onto, and I want it to be as sharp and aggressive as possible.”.

In a recent development, “I would make sure you have enough hole patterns to make a lot of adjustments. Sometimes, they’re too spaced out, for example, in two-inch increments instead of one,” Sevcik notes. “I like to have the added adjustability, especially for those heavier weights.”.

It has been revealed that sevcik notes having the option to do pull-ups is a good idea. “They’re one of the most basic, fundamental movements. Plus, if you dedicate the square footage to put the rack in there, you’ll want to get as much utility as possible because you are sacrificing some real estate.”.

“It’s crucial to have the option to add accessories,” Sevcik says. “You might not want a dip bar right now, but down the road, you may decide to incorporate more dips in the training program, and it sure is nice to have your power rack as your one central piece of equipment.”.

Many power racks come with attachments, though certain brands require you to purchase add-on attachments separately. Some of the power racks on this list come with pull-up bars (chin-up bar), safeties, and J-cups included, while others do not. It’s important to read the details of what comes with your unit to know what additional purchases you’ll need to make to achieve your desired power rack workout.

We considered the following while choosing each product on this list:.

We chose budget-friendly and high-end options suitable for any fitness level and listed several compact and folding options for those with limited space. We also spoke to Shane Sevcik, a USAW-certified coach and competitive athlete, about essential add-ons and safety features.

Research suggests 30 to 60 minutes a week of muscle-strengthening exercises can benefit your health. With the help of a power rack, you can achieve a wide range of strength training fitness moves without needing a spotter. A power rack can add convenience to your workout by enabling you to get a safe weightlifting workout anytime from the comfort of your home gym.

A full power rack has four to six uprights attached by cross members, creating a cage to lift in. A squat rack—also called a squat stand—is typically two uprights and weighs less than a power rack, making it more portable. Power racks are more versatile, with the option to add accessories, while squat racks usually do not.

If you choose a freestanding power rack, anchor it following the manufacturer’s instructions to ensure it’s safe and secure.

Sources indicate that generally, a freestanding power rack should be a few feet from the wall so you can perform exercises comfortably and safely. Always refer to the manufacturer’s guidelines and recommendations when setting up your rack.

Sources indicate that common gauges are 11-gauge and 12-gauge, with lower numbers providing thicker and stronger steel; however, these tend to be more pricey options. A thinner 14-gauge steel is slightly less sturdy but likely works well for a general home gym setup. We chose racks ranging from 11-gauge to 16-gauge to suit various budgets and fitness levels.

Whether you’re buying a latest e-bike for yourself or a gift for a partner, spouse, or family member, this is your chance to score the best deal of 2026.

E-bikes are also great for your daily commute, basic transportation, and running errands.

No matter your budget or riding needs—from commuters to mountain bikers, experienced cyclists and brand-new riders—there is an e-bike for everyone and every age. Our test team rides dozens of electric bikes each year, and these are some of our favorites and the best deals out there right now.

➜ AMAZON ➜ REI ➜ BACKCOUNTRY ➜ COMPETITIVE CYCLIST ➜ SPECIALIZED ➜ TREK ➜ CANNONDALE ➜ AVENTON ➜ LECTRIC ➜ SEGWAY ➜ RIDE1UP ➜ VELOTRIC.

Industry observers note that the Aventon Level is our benchmark electric bike. It’s a great e-bike for commuting, running errands, or leisure riding. The Level platform has proven to be reliable, low-maintenance, and fun to ride—and it doesn’t break the bank.

The REC features a 750W hub motor with 80 Nm of torque. The bike also has regenerative braking, upping the range to 75 miles. For commutes and running errands, the Level comes standard with fenders, a rear rack, lights, and suspension.

Riders will also find the Level’s connected features very useful. The Level 4’s ACU (Aventon Control Unit) adds several smart features to the already well-equipped platform. The wheel lock and motion sensor alarm are passive theft deterrents when you stop for a mid-ride coffee or run into the post office. A 4G chip in the ACU enables GPS tracking in Aventon’s mobile app, so you can locate your bike if you forget where you locked it. 4G connectivity also allows you to set geofence restrictions on the bike for teens or housemates.

It has been revealed that compared with earlier Aventure versions, the third-generation model rides smoother and feels more like a premium bike (without the high price tag). Aventon’s fresh torque sensor allows more control over the acceleration of Aventure’s 750W rear hub motor. Lighter-weight testers found previous models had too much torque, but Aventure fixed that issue. Additional features include a new head-unit interface, integrated turn signals, a front light, a rear rack, and fenders.

The Aventure 3 is an excellent fat-tire e-bike for commuters—especially on snowy days and gravel paths. Off-road, it excels on doubletrack trails and cinder paths. However, the bike is burly; its weight and components limit its fun on technical singletrack and more aggressive mountain trails.

Aventon also offers a mid-drive version of the Aventure. It keeps the same big, burly character but adds a more premium feel, a smoother, more powerful motor, and an upgraded drivetrain—along with a higher price.

Aventon’s Pace 5 REC is a zippy e-bike that’s perfect for weekend cruises around town, the bike path, or even occasional commutes. The brand refined the Pace with a slew of updates, making it one of the best bang-for-your-buck step-throughs on the market. These include connected features (such as GPS tracking and theft deterrence), a powerful 750 Watt motor, regenerative braking, and an impressive 75-mile range. It’s offered in five colors (grey, mint, pink, orange, and teal) and two frame sizes.

The Pace 5 does not come with a rack, fenders, or a suspension fork. If you commute by bike frequently or use your e-bike for running errands, consider paying $200 more for the Level 4.

A 2024 Bicycling Bike Awards winner, the Cervélo Rouvida is an electric gravel bike that looks and handles like a traditional analog bike—but with a little extra kick. That performance comes from the tiny-but-mighty Fazua motor; the 250-watt/60 N/m Ride 60 system blends smooth feel and good power (especially in Rocket mode). The unit produces a little bit of noise, but it’s less than many other e-bike motors—it’s audible enough that you hear it working, but it’s not annoying or distracting. This is a great bike for getting in gravel or road rides in the winter when you’re pressed for time due to darkness or cold temps.

Industry observers note that electric mountain bikes are a ton of fun and are quickly becoming the go-to choice for performance-minded off-road riders. However, a downside to trail-worthy E-MTBs is often cost: even “budget” models can cost upwards of $5,000, and high-end models often cost more than $10,000.

That’s what makes this deal pretty sweet: The Instinct Powerplay SL C70 features a lightweight carbon frame, 29-inch wheels, Fox Performance Elite suspension, and SRAM GX wireless drivetrain with Code brakes. At the heart of this E-MTB is a lightweight 700-watt/75 Nm motor system, developed in-house by Rocky Mountain in Canada.

Buying an e-bike on Amazon can be risky, especially if you don’t know much about bikes or have much mechanical experience. However, sometimes you can find a good deal on a decent bike. At $500, the Heybike Cityscape isn’t the pinnacle of e-bike tech, but it helps you get out and enjoy some rides without busting your budget.

Industry observers note that the Cityscape stands out for its combination of low price, practical features (like a rack and fenders), and a UL-certified battery. Unlike some Amazon brands, Heybike offers a U.S. support line for warranty service or product questions.

Includes FREE accessories: Running Boards, Frame Bag, Cushions, Elite Headlight, Seatpost, Comfort Seat, and Orbitor.

Many riders are attracted to the XPedition’s very appealing price. Discounted to $1,699, the dual-battery model has up to 120 miles of range and a 28 mph top speed. A single-battery version is also available for $1,399; it boasts an impressive 60-mile range. Need even more battery power? The $1,999 Long Range model goes up to 170 miles from a single charge.

These prices make the XPedition one of the most affordable electric cargo bikes on the market. And they’re a solid option for riders seeking an excellent deal on an e-cargo bike. “The XPedition’s capability surprised me”, stated Test Editor Dan Chabanov. “Combined with the Lectric XL panniers and the Essentials package, I comfortably carried several days of groceries for a family of three or one adult passenger.”.

Includes FREE accessories: Rear Rack, Water-Resistant Panniers, Lock, Elite Headlight, Seatpost, Comfort Saddle, Phone Mount, and Mirrors.

Recent findings suggest that if you want power and range in a small package, the XP4 750 is right for you. It’s a fast, zippy Class 3 e-bike (pedal assist up to 28 mph) with a 330-pound payload capacity. To increase the XP4’s function and fun, the 750 has a 1310-watt peak motor output (200 watts more than the standard model) and an 85-mile range.

Whether you’re riding city streets on your commute or out for a weekend ride, this bike is fast, easy to ride, and a blast to pedal.

Includes FREE accessories: Rear Rack, Fenders, Headlight, and Seatpost.

The XP Lite 2.0 scales back the XP4 750’s top speed and power, with pedal assist topping out at 20 mph, a peak motor output of 819 watts, and a reduced payload capacity of 275 pounds. It also drops the suspension fork found on the XP4, but still delivers an impressive range of up to 80 miles.

It has been revealed that however, the XP Lite isn’t simply a stripped-down version of the XP4; it has some major advantages. At 49 pounds (without accessories and options), it’s 26 pounds lighter than the higher-powered model. This makes the Lite much easier to lift and transport. Plus, instead of an 8-speed drivetrain, the XP Lite features a low-maintenance Gates belt drive. That means no greasy chain, no finicky gear adjustments, and a quieter, cleaner ride. Yes, it’s a singlespeed, but the pedal-assist motor easily compensates for all but the steepest hills or heaviest loads.

Includes FREE accessories: Support Seat, Elite Headlight, Suspension Seatpost, and Cargo Package.

In a recent development, electric trikes are a great choice for many riders, including seniors, people with mobility limitations, and those who need to carry heavy payloads. At $1,699, the Lectric XP Trike2 is an easy-to-ride, stable three-wheeler.

A 750-watt motor with 1,310 peak watts powers the XP Trike up to 17 mph and up to 70 miles of range on a charge. The Trike features a wide, soft seat with back support. Plus, it has a suspension seatpost and suspension fork for added comfort.

Need a lightweight e-bike for city riding, your last-mile commute, or carrying in your car or RV? If so, Brompton’s C-Line Electric 4-speed is your answer. This lightweight (36.5-pound) folding e-bike packs down tiny and can be carried on most trains and buses. Made in England, Brompton bikes have earned a cult following for their quirky-yet-functional design and excellent engineering. And at 20% off, this is a great deal.

Sources indicate that with a top speed of 28 mph, 81 miles of range, a 100mm-travel suspension fork, 27.5”x2.6”, a rack, and fenders, the Adventure Neo Allroad Speed’s name fits it to a T. This bike is built for adventures large and small, from commutes to work in the snow or rain, to gravel trails at your local park.

Recent findings suggest that to power the Adventure, Cannondale uses a Bafang 750W rear hub motor and an easy-access 750 Wh removable battery. With its power and wide-range 8-speed drivetrain, you will get up every hill, while Tektro hydraulic disc brakes will control your speed on descents. Plus, it’s available in flashy red or more subdued matte black.

At $1,200, this Cannondale is 45% off its original price and is equipped with better parts than many lesser-known brands’ bikes priced hundreds more.

Many “step-through” e-bikes lack a truly low-step design, making them difficult for some riders to mount or dismount. However, the CTY e2.1, from REI’s Co-op house brand, has a fully step-through front triangle. This makes the CTY a great choice for older riders, those with mobility limitations, or others who seek an easy-to-ride e-bike.

REI equips the CTY e2.1 with a 250-watt hub-drive motor; it provides smooth pedal assistance up to 20 mph. It also features a suspension fork to smooth out bumps and potholes, an adjustable stem to custom-tune your riding position, and hydraulic disc brakes for improved stopping power. For less than the cost of many unknown e-bikes online, you can get a quality electric bike backed up by REI’s warranty and service.

In a recent development, salsa’s Moraine 145 costs less than many hardtail E-MTBs. But don’t let the price fool you; this bike is value-packed. This dual 29-inch-wheeled trail bike comes equipped with Fazua’s Ride 60 motor (60 Newton-meters of torque) and a 430-Watt-hour battery. While it has less torque and a smaller-capacity battery than higher-priced competitors, it has enough power for some serious fun in the woods and on singletrack.

The frame uses a Split Pivot suspension system designed by Dave Weagle (the mastermind behind the dw-link suspension system on Pivot bikes), for a balance of performance and pedalability. A 10-speed Shimano Cues drivetrain, four-piston Shimano brakes, a dropper post, and Terravail tubeless tires round out the components of this feature-packed full-suspension E-MTB.

Recent findings suggest that electric bikes are great for commuting and city life. However, their added weight (sometimes as much as 90 or 100 pounds) can make e-bikes a pain to carry up flights of stairs, load onto a bus or train, or even move around in your garage.

It has been revealed that weighing only about 40 pounds, the Roadster v3 cuts weight without sacrificing much performance or adding cost. Ride1Up uses a 500 watt/50Nm rear hub motor with an internal battery for a clean, stealthy look. 700x45c gravel tires carry speed on pavement or hardpack dirt roads, and metal fenders keep the road spray off your clothes.

Industry observers note that many people know Segway for its original electric stand-up people mover. But did you know the brand also makes e-bikes? Segway offers several electric-assist mini-cargo and commuter bike models, including the sleek Muxi Pro. It also has handy smart features (like traction control, Apple Find My, and hill descent control), plus a 750-watt hub motor with 80 Nm of torque.

Sources indicate that this is an absolutely bananas deal for the right rider! If you can ride a size XL frame, you can get a Specialized Turbo Vado SL 4.0—an e-bike that typically sells for $3,500—for less than $1,000. It features Specialized’s excellent Turbo SL 1.1 motor, a 320 Wh internal battery, an 11-speed SRAM drivetrain, and a Lezyne headlight. Run, don’t walk to get this deal!

Recent findings suggest that over the last 18 months, I’ve probably ridden the Specialized Turbo Vado SL 2 on more days than any other bike. That’s because it’s a super-reliable commuter bike with a great motor, spot-on handling and geometry, and includes extras like a rack, fenders, and lights. At 25 percent off its everyday price, this Turbo Vado doesn’t cost a lot more than some bikes from consumer-direct brands—but you get a higher-performance bike. And it’s often worth paying more on an e-bike to ensure performance and serviceability.

According to recent reports, electric mountain bikes are a ton of fun and help you ride more of your favorite trails. We recommend full-suspension E-MTBs for aggressive and technical trails. But hardtails often work fine on easier trails and mellower terrain, and they cost a lot less than dual-suspension models.

Sources indicate that velotric keeps costs low on the Summit 1 by using a rear hub motor instead of a pricier mid-drive unit. The Summit also features an 8-speed Shimano drivetrain rather than more expensive 11- or 12-speed systems. However, Velotric gives the bike a 120mm thru-axle fork to soak up bumps, Shimano hydraulic disc brakes, and a full-color screen with Bluetooth connectivity.

Recent findings suggest that many electric bikes exceed 60 or 80 pounds, so a sub-40-pound e-bike is rather impressive. Unfortunately, e-bikes this light are usually rather expensive. However, Velotric’s Tempo only costs $1,399 and boasts a 39 lb. (claimed) weight. Velotric achieves this weight reduction and low cost by ditching the bulky suspension fork and using a smaller battery.

Like most hybrids, and unlike many e-bikes, the Tempo features 700c gravel tires. These tires roll quicker than 26- or 27.5-inch tires on pavement while giving the Tempo improved traction on dirt roads and gravel paths. Velotric offers the Tempo in a traditional double diamond frame and a mid-step design. Both frames are available in two colors and two sizes.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that getting to the Philadelphia Marathon on November 22 proved an endurance event of its own for Travis Meier. The 38-year-old Minneapolis resident flew into Hartford, Connecticut, drove three hours into the Adirondack Mountains to pick up a canoe, then spent another five hours behind the wheel getting to Philadelphia. This was all before tackling Sunday’s 26.2 miles with the boat balanced over his head.

And yes, the canoe made it through the entire race without ever touching water.

In a recent development, “Coming from Minnesota, I can't just throw a boat in an overhead compartment," Meier told Runner's World. "It was a logistical nightmare: where to keep it, where to sneak it into the race, and how people would react to it.".

Despite the travel headaches, Meier came away from Philadelphia with his second personal record in as many weeks. It was another step in his latest undertaking: 52 marathons in 52 weeks, each while carrying a canoe, to raise awareness about protecting the Boundary Waters Canoe Area Wilderness in northern Minnesota.

According to recent reports, meier, who manages a distillery when he isn't hauling boats around, wasn't exactly a seasoned runner when all this started. His introduction to the sport came through the Red Bull Urban Portage, an event that involved carrying a boat through downtown Minneapolis before paddling along the Mississippi River.

Recent findings suggest that “I was really bad at paddling, but I could outrun people,” he recalled. Before the event, he bought a Northstar ADK canoe off Craigslist with every intention of selling it once the race was over. Instead, it found a home on his garage wall and managed to stick around for another year. Eventually, he started entering more races with it.

It has been revealed that that eventually brought him to Minnesota's Ely Marathon in 2023, where he completed his first-ever 26.2-mile race while carrying a canoe. Since then, he's run only one conventional marathon without a boat, and what started solely as a personal experiment gradually became an opportunity to draw attention to a place he'd loved for years.

Sources indicate that the Boundary Waters, a wilderness area known for its lakes, forests, and extensive canoe routes, has been at the center of a contentious debate over proposed mining operations. Federal protections restricting mining in the surrounding watershed were rolled back earlier this year, a development that particularly frustrated Meier.

"I've been to many remote places on this earth, and very few have its caliber of perfect,” he said. “So why would someone want to mess it up?".

It has been revealed that meier had been toying with the idea of running 52 marathons in 52 weeks ever since reading about Dane Rauschenberg, who accomplished the feat in 2006. With the ongoing fight over protections for the Boundary Waters, he had his reason to give it a shot, bringing his canoe as a form of protest to May’s Taco Bell 50K. It got people asking questions, which was exactly what he wanted, and gave him encouragement to keep showing up at races with a boat on his head.

Of course, carrying a canoe for more than four hours at a time comes with some challenges, particularly when Mother Nature gets involved.

According to recent reports, during the Mankato Marathon in Minnesota, Meier battled 30mph winds along a ridge beside a cornfield. Mile 14 alone took him nearly 22 minutes, as his canoe repeatedly caught the wind and spun him around like a kite.

According to recent reports, at one point, Meier turned to a few supporters witnessing him get thrown around and asked, “When's the point of insanity?” He sent them ahead to see if the wind conditions were better ahead in the valley. Luckily, the gusts let up enough, sparing him a repeat trip through that nightmare.

The spectators in Philadelphia offered a different kind of entertainment, with plenty to say about the guy running a marathon with a canoe on his head.

Around mile three, Meier encountered a young girl who appeared scared by the enormous object approaching her. He knelt down, giving her enough confidence to return his high-five.

"Grandmas confess their love to me, and I don't know why," he mentioned of his interactions with spectators, adding that Philadelphia set a record for the number of phallic jokes he heard along the course.

It has been revealed that the jokes are part of the experience, and the attention is ultimately what he's hoping for. Meier stated fellow runners often approach him after a race to discuss the Boundary Waters and the larger concern of protecting public lands. He's also seen Instagram comments from people who knew little about the area before coming across his videos.

"They may not know anything, but they've at least gotten a 10,000-foot view of the BWCA," he said.

In a recent development, the running community has helped make the challenge possible, with sponsors pitching in for race entries and shoes while Meier covers the remaining expenses. He's even promised to refund their donations if he doesn't complete the challenge.

"My integrity is everything,” he said, “even though I'm not a company, just a guy with a boat on his head.”.

Industry observers note that his biggest sacrifice so far has been giving up so much of his free time. Between a full-time job, travel, recovery, and the weekly races, there’s no room for a vacation abroad. He has considered tackling back-to-back marathons to create some breathing room. His body hasn't agreed to the arrangement.

It has been revealed that as for what would make all 52 races worthwhile, Meier has a specific outcome in mind: permanent legislation protecting the Boundary Waters. Here’s the good news: proposals exist in both the House of Representatives and Senate. Even so, he knows that may be a tall order. But his presence—and effort—are creating awareness.

"If it doesn't happen, which it likely won't, at least the effort started conversations about our public lands," he stated.

It has been revealed that sean Abrams was the Senior Editor, Growth and Engagement at Men’s Health. He’s a former hip hop dancer who likes long walks on the beach and large glasses of tequila. You can find his previous work at Maxim, Elite Daily, and AskMen.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, elliptical machines have come a long way, with major developments in specs and technology. Their ergonomic design maximizes the quality and intensity of your workout, incorporating both upper and lower body muscles. This provides you with a full-body workout to enhance your cardio fitness while maintaining the structural integrity of your joints. We consider that an all-around win.

If you are on the hunt for the best elliptical of 2025 but aren’t sure where to start, you’ve come to the right place. Below, you’ll find our top picks for the best elliptical machines and a comprehensive guide on what to consider before you make your purchase.

It has been revealed that the NordicTrack FS10i isn’t your average elliptical—it combines a treadmill, elliptical, and stair stepper all into one machine designed to give you the flexibility to switch up your cardio. The 32-inch adjustable stride adjusts based on your leg movements. In other words, if you use the FS10i as a stair stepper, your legs move up and down, but your stride goes back and forth in elliptical mode.

It has been revealed that you can follow an iFIT class (with a $39/month subscription) on the 10-inch HD touchscreen, which tracks key stats such as time elapsed, speed, distance, and calories burned. Trainers can digitally adjust your incline up to 10 percent or tap into the 24 resistance levels based on the workout. If you’re working out manually, you can make these adjustments yourself via one-touch buttons next to the touchscreen.

Recent findings suggest that if you’re on a fitness journey, a weight-loss diet and exercise are essential to achieving your goals. If you already have a favorite weight-loss program or weight-loss app, an elliptical can help you knock out your daily sweat session. While any elliptical will help you work toward your goal, the E95 stands out thanks to its free fitness app and integrated streaming services, perfect for when you need more motivation to get moving. Unlike some of the other ellipticals on our list, the E95’s companion app, Sole+, is free with your new machine. Sole+ includes more than 3,000 trainer-led workouts and classes for on and off your elliptical. For even more entertainment while you work out, the E95 is integrated with several streaming services, including Netflix, Amazon Prime, Hulu, and more.

The Sole E95’s cushioned foot pedals are designed to keep your knees and ankles from feeling the brunt of an extended workout. The pedals adjust to fit your gait, but default to a two-degree inward angle. The Sole E95’s 20 resistance levels let you challenge yourself and can be easily switched via buttons on the handles. Sole’s drive system is engineered to stay quiet, but if you want to listen to your class or music on its built-in speakers, simply plug in your smart device and prop it up in the inserted tablet holder.

RELATED: Best Home Gym Equipment.

The Sole E35 Elliptical is a great choice for anyone looking for a reliable, simple elliptical with a smooth ride for joint comfort. It’s easy to set up and use and has everything you need to start working out in the comfort of your own home—no gym membership required.

The Sole E35’s ramp-like design allows users to simply step on and start moving. With this elliptical, you can get a full-body workout without having to worry about straining your back or joints. It is equipped with 20 different levels of resistance so users can adjust their workouts according to their fitness levels and goals. With 10 preloaded workout programs plus free access to the Sole+ fitness app, even beginners can start their training immediately. Even though it’s not as heavy-duty as other ellipticals, the  Sole E35 works for users up to 300 pounds.

And while it comes with all the features you’d expect from an elliptical, it also has some great extras that we love: built-in fans keep you cool during workouts, and a user-friendly, fully adjustable console ensures a comfortable workout.

RELATED: Best Budget Home Gym Equipment.

If you’re short on space but looking to up your cardio workout with an elliptical, take a look at the Bowflex Max Trainer M6. Bringing together form and function, the M6 stamps out a footprint measuring just 46 inches long, 26 inches wide, and 64.2 inches high—quite a bit smaller than your average treadmill or other cardio machine. Its 15-inch stride length may not be a great fit for taller individuals, but it still supports a user weight of up to 300 pounds.

Sources indicate that the M6 offers a great workout with 16 levels of resistance, a USB charging port, a water bottle holder, Bluetooth heart rate compatibility, and multi-grip moving handles with pulse contact grips to measure heart rate. It’s also equipped with a unique burn rate display to track how many calories you burn per minute and allows you to set activity level targets throughout the workout.

Industry observers note that if interactive programming is your jam, you’re in luck. The JRNY digital fitness platform for Bowflex products houses tailored workouts, on-demand classes, real-time coaching, and personalized programming. Purchasing the M6 gives you a free membership to JRNY. Download the workout app, place your device in the magnetic media, and get pedaling.

Industry observers note that bowflex offers in-home assembly for an additional fee, which we recommend because assembly takes a few hours (according to reviewers). The warranty is a bit disappointing, offering only two years on the frame and parts. Most competitors cover the frame with a 10-year warranty, so you’ll want to make sure your Bowflex is assembled correctly.

According to recent reports, the little elliptical that could, the Cubii Go provides an elliptical experience for a fraction of the space and price. This portable elliptical fits seamlessly underneath your desk and can be taken on the go with its built-in wheels and retractable handle.

Unlike under-desk treadmills, you don’t have to stand to work out with the Cubii Go. Instead, you can stay seated and pedal during a meeting or while watching TV. Its large flywheel lets you go up to ten resistance levels while an illuminated display projects your stats back to you. Use the Cubii app to keep track of the details of your workout plus. The Cubii Go is also easy to take with you, thanks to built-in wheels and a double telescoping handle.

Sources indicate that this compact elliptical right now has an average rating of 4.8 out of 5 stars on the Cubii website. Out of 238 reviews, only five give the Cubii Go one star. Negative ratings include criticism of the machine’s stability and design. Four-star reviews praise the Cubii Go as effective and easy to use.

If you’re a first-time elliptical buyer who’s feeling a little intimidated by the whole process, you might find the Niceday Smart Elliptical CT11 a comfortable option. Equipped with large pedals and constructed with steel, the Niceday Elliptical trainer can support consumers up to 400 pounds. It’s also designed to fit users between 4’9″ and 6’4″ tall, although it’s worth noting that the 15.5-inch stride length may feel restrictive to people on the taller end of that range. This elliptical also comes 90 percent pre-assembled, a feature sure to appeal to those less mechanically inclined. If you find quiet workouts comfortable, you’ll appreciate the Smart Elliptical CT11’s magnetic drive system. It’s designed to reduce noise and keep the sound of the machine below 20 decibels—about the same amount of noise as rustling leaves.

Recent findings suggest that this elliptical trainer offers 16 levels of resistance, so you can use it for anything from light workouts to more intense leg and glute exercises. It’s also compatible with Kinomap and digitally records stats including speed, distance, calories, and heart rate.

Sources indicate that the Niceday Smart Elliptical CT11 has an average rating of 4.4 out of 5 stars on Amazon with nearly 3,000 reviews. While most Amazon feedback is complimentary about the machine’s performance, criticisms include noise level and suitability for taller customers.

Elliptical machines are an excellent choice for people looking for a low-impact, total-body cardio workout of any intensity. “You’re using both your arms and your legs to propel yourself, and you can adjust the resistance based on what works for you,” claims Samantha April, P.T., D.P.T., U.S.A.-W. They’re also great for people with balance issues. “Someone may use an elliptical over a treadmill if they’re looking for something that’s a little more controlled and they want to move with the machine and keep their feet stationary versus a treadmill where they’re required to move,” says April.

Recent findings suggest that however, elliptical machines are not ideal for people with small home gym spaces. “If space is a concern inside of your home gym, ellipticals take up a pretty fair amount of space, so it’s vital that you’ll actually have the space to accommodate that,” April indicates.

Customers can do a variety of workouts on an elliptical trainer, from slow, easy walks to fast and intense interval sessions.

Recent findings suggest that don’t forget to warm up with some deep breaths and stretching. When you’re ready, place your feet on the pedals and grab the handles. Begin moving your feet forward in a general walking motion.

It has been revealed that although you’re free to go at your own pace, a good baseline for elliptical workouts is 15-20 minutes. As you get more comfortable and build your endurance, you can increase your speed, resistance, and incline (if your machine has variable incline settings).

We asked Matt Petrillo, C.S.C.S., director of adult fitness at The Annex Sports Performance in Passaic, N.J., how to get a great workout on the elliptical.

It has been revealed that “My clients utilize ellipticals through low-intensity interval training. To do this, choose a work interval ranging from 30-90 seconds and a rest interval between 30-60 seconds, making sure your work period is longer than your rest,” Petrillo says.

Industry observers note that he says when you are in your work period, you want to begin each round with your heart rate as close to 120 beats per minute as possible. By the end of your work period, you want your heart rate to be between 150-160 beats per minute.

“During your rest period, the goal is to drop your heart rate to as close to 120 beats per minute as possible,” states Petrillo. Don’t have a heart rate monitor? That’s OK, too. “Simply go at the fastest sustainable pace you can while only breathing through your nose during your work periods,” Petrillo says.

Depending on fitness level and time constraints, go through the work/rest process for 15-30 rounds. “This type of workout helps build our aerobic system, which can greatly improve our cardiovascular and overall health,” Petrillo claims.

To help you choose the best elliptical for your needs and goals, we evaluated dozens of machines and looked at several factors, including:.

Industry observers note that the flywheel is the heavy, rotating wheel inside your machine. It provides stability and momentum while you pedal. A heavier flywheel offers a better, smoother ride and is generally more expensive.

It has been revealed that A range of resistance levels is vital for workout intensity variability and training progression. Ellipticals function on a fixed track, so increasing speed is limited.

You’ll want an elliptical with enough resistance options for challenging workouts as your physical fitness improves.

In a recent development, incline ranges on an elliptical are more of an added bonus than a must-have. They can add a level of variability to training. By increasing or decreasing the slope, you activate different muscle groups and change the intensity of the workout without necessarily changing speed or resistance. As the slope increases, more output is required from the user to generate speed, which will increase heart rate. It’s similar to walking up a hill versus walking on flat ground.

Recent findings suggest that stride length refers to how far apart the pedals move from one another when in use. The stride length most affects how comfortable and natural the stride feels for you. A short stride length will feel cramped to anyone with longer legs or particularly long strides. Conversely, a large stride length may feel awkward and clunky to someone with short legs. There is no universal best stride length since it’s highly dependent on your leg length and overall height. Most ellipticals feature a 20-inch stride length, which works for the vast majority of people.

Recent findings suggest that if you live in a small apartment or are equipping a tiny home gym space, you’ll want a compact elliptical that occupies minimal real estate. Measure out the space where you plan to use your elliptical before you start your search.

If you’re a sucker for technology and place a premium on programming with top-of-the-line features and conveniences, make sure you find an elliptical that checks off all your boxes. Write out a list of your must-have technology specifications and features before you begin your search. This will help you narrow down your focus and streamline the process.

Industry observers note that this may seem like a no-brainer, but knowing your budget is imperative when buying any type of home exercise equipment. Ellipticals come at a variety of price points, from a few hundred dollars to several thousand.

It has been revealed that elliptical cross trainers are a great way to improve your cardio fitness and strength. The combination of the resistance from the pedals and handlebars provides you with a full-body workout.

Treadmills and elliptical trainers are great ways to get aerobic exercise. Choosing between them primarily depends on your fitness goals, your current fitness level, and whether you have an existing injury or condition that affects your joints or muscles. Consider these factors:-A full-size elliptical provides a full-body workout that targets your arms and shoulders in addition to your legs, calves, and glutes.-Ellipticals are not as high-impact since your feet remain in contact with the pedals rather than repeatedly striking the running deck of a treadmill. If you have joint pain or a lower-body injury, an elliptical will probably put less stress on those areas.-A treadmill makes more sense if you’re focused on building endurance and leg strength. It’s the better choice for runners and walkers.-The learning curve with an elliptical machine could be more difficult since it involves more complex movements than simply running or walking.Other factors besides workouts could also affect your decision. For example, treadmills tend to be more expensive than ellipticals. A high-quality elliptical trainer will almost certainly be less noisy than a treadmill, an vital consideration for home workouts.

How many calories you burn depends on your body size, fitness level, and the intensity and duration of your workout. However, according to Harvard Health Publishing, users can expect to burn between 270–370 calories for 30 minutes of exercise on an elliptical machine.

Recent findings suggest that yes, but not specifically. While it’s impossible to target fat burning in specific areas of your body, exercising on an elliptical machine, when paired with a weight-loss diet, can help consumers maintain a calorie deficit, contributing to all-over fat loss.

It has been revealed that consistency and accountability are crucial when it comes to weight loss. The best elliptical for weight loss is the machine you use regularly. Look for an elliptical with features to keep you motivated and focused. However, proper nutrition is just as vital as having a consistent workout schedule.

Industry observers note that yes. The elliptical works both the upper body and lower body, targeting your glutes, quadriceps, hamstrings, calves, arms, and core.

It has been revealed that walking and the elliptical are cardio workouts. Typically, ellipticals enable you to burn more calories with varied intensities, resistance, and preset workout options. Ellipticals are easier on your joints than walking, offering a solid alternative to the impact of walking on pavement or a treadmill.

Seeing results from any form of exercise depends on your goals and the effort you put into your workouts.

We Had Too Many Pumpkin Spice Gels, So Naturally We Turned Them Into a Pie

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (819 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Bicycling

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that gear-obsessed editors choose every product we review.
  • Recently at the Bicycling office, I was looking at all of the nutrition supplies that I had sitting around.
  • This is the first pie I’ve successfully baked in my life, so it seems only fitting that I would make my first pie out of nutrition I take on rides.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that gear-obsessed editors choose every product we review. We may earn commission if you buy from a link. How we test gear.

Recently at the Bicycling office, I was looking at all of the nutrition supplies that I had sitting around. I sit next to Tara Seplavy, Bicycling’s Deputy Test Editor, and I noticed between her stash and mine we had a healthy stockpile of GU Pumpkin Spice gels. Especially with Thanksgiving coming up, the thought crept in, I should make a pumpkin pie out of that.

This is the first pie I’ve successfully baked in my life, so it seems only fitting that I would make my first pie out of nutrition I take on rides. Before making the pie, I was doubtful that it would be edible, but our Test Editor Dan Chabanov had confidence it would come out reasonably well.

Here I’ll go through how the final product turned out and include the recipe so you can make this for your Thanksgiving group ride.

Usually I’m not a fan of eating gels when I ride—typically I opt for drink mixes to get in the fuel that I need to keep pedaling. It’s mostly a texture issue when I’m trying to get gels down during a ride, so I was hesitant to think I would enjoy the final product of this experiment.

It would have been unrealistic to expect the filling would be the same as a regular pumpkin pie, but to my surprise it was much closer than I expected. I anticipated it would be a soupy mess in a pie crust, but the texture of the final product reminded me more cheesecake. Don’t get me wrong—it is a little stickier than a regular pumpkin pie. But I wouldn’t guess this was made out of gels if I didn’t make it myself.

It has been revealed that the flavor was better than expected, too. This experiment made me realize that I’ve been trying to fuel with gels wrong all these years. I shouldn’t have been trying to slurp them out of a little packet. All I had to do was bake a handful of gels into a pie.

According to recent reports, coming up with the recipe was hard—believe it or not, everyone I know that has baking experience had no idea how to help give guidance when making a pie out of gels and drink mix. So, I asked ChatGPT to whip me up a recipe—that seems like the best use case for artificial intelligence, right? From there I made some tweaks and got to work.

Bonus to all of this? My house still smells like pumpkin spice and now I have fuel for all my activities this weekend. After this successful test, I can’t help but think what other baked goods I could make with gels—stay tuned.

It has been revealed that step-by-Step Directions   1. Prep the oven: Place a rack in the lower-middle position and heat the oven to 400°F. 2. Dissolve the recovery mix: In a medium to large mixing bowl, squeeze in the 8 GU Pumpkin Spice gels and whisk in the ½ cup cold water until completely smooth. 3. Whisk the base: Mix in the 2 scoops of the GU Vanilla Roctane Recovery Mix. Let it sit for 2 minutes so the foam settles. Then whisk in the 3 eggs until uniform. 4. Combine remaining ingredients: Add the 4 tablespoons cornstarch, 2 tablespoons melted butter, ¼ teaspoon salt, and optional cinnamon, whisking until smooth and pourable. (If the batter looks thicker than heavy pancake batter, whisk in 1 to 2 tablespoons of extra water). 5. Initial high-heat bake: Pour the filling into the unbaked pie crust. Bake at 400°F for 12 minutes to set the bottom crust. 6. Finish baking gently: Without opening the oven door, reduce the temperature to 325°F. Bake for another 30 to 40 minutes, until the outer 2 inches of filling are puffed and set, while the very center still jiggles like gelatin when gently nudged. (If the crust edges brown too quickly, cover them loosely with foil). 7. Cool and chill: Remove the pie from the oven and let it cool completely to room temperature on a wire rack (about 1.5 to 2 hours). Transfer to the refrigerator and chill for at least 4 hours (or overnight) so the cornstarch fully sets before slicing. I opted for overnight so it would be ready for my morning heat session on the trainer.

Lately though, his toughest balancing act has been fitting trainer rides between family life and the next adventure.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Creatine is a popular muscle-building supplement, and for good reason.
  • Sources indicate that there are tons of creatine supplements on the market, including powders, pills, and gummies.
  • It has been revealed that on one hand, having such a wide variety of options can be empowering.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Creatine is a popular muscle-building supplement, and for good reason. It’s one of the most research-backed supplements for muscle growth and recovery. While some people associate creatine with weightlifters or bodybuilders, it’s a great supplement for anyone looking to build muscle, enhance their performance, and promote better recovery.

Sources indicate that there are tons of creatine supplements on the market, including powders, pills, and gummies. These supplements use various forms of creatine (more on that later), and some contain other ingredients that aim to help you grow muscle, recover faster, or sharpen your focus in the gym.

It has been revealed that on one hand, having such a wide variety of options can be empowering. On the other hand, it can be a challenge to figure out which is right for you.

It has been revealed that to narrow down the field to only the best of the best, our expert product testers tried dozens of creatine supplements ranging from standard powders to convenient capsules to flavorful gummies. We looked for creatine supplements that taste good, mix well (when applicable), use quality ingredients, contain enough creatine per serving, and are affordable. Along the way, we spoke with certified personal trainers and nutritionists for guidance.

Below are our picks for the best creatine supplements for men. However, individuals of any gender can choose from this lineup with confidence.

Disclaimer: While this article is intended for educational and informational purposes, it should not be viewed as a substitute for medical advice. Furthermore, we intend the term “men” to include all men, including trans men. However, we understand most research on this topic has focused on cis men (men who are not trans). When we reference gender-based research and nutritional recommendations, we will clarify by saying “cis men.” We encourage trans and nonbinary people of all genders to consult with a trans-competent nutritionist regarding their supplements and training needs.

Industry observers note that transparent Labs Creatine HMB is our pick for the best creatine monohydrate because it contains 5 grams of it per serving, which is the researched-backed dose for improved athletic performance. “This dose is a great recommendation for the general population, but some sports nutrition recommendations recommend a dosage based on kilograms of body weight, so some individuals may require more than 5 grams to see a benefit,” says Anna Marie Clear, M.S., R.D., C.P.T.

This dietary supplement contains β-hydroxy β-methylbutyrate (HMB), which the body naturally produces when it breaks down the amino acid leucine. Although more studies are needed, some research suggests HMB promotes muscle growth. “Leucine is the primary amino acid that triggers muscle protein synthesis,” Clear explains.”HMB and leucine are very similar, but research shows HMB has no greater effect than leucine alone.”.

Sources indicate that transparent Labs also includes BioPerine, a derivative of black pepper that studies show increases nutrient bioavailability. “Bioperine may help enhance absorption of some nutrients, but research is limited on its impact alongside HMB and creatine,” indicates Clear.

Sources indicate that earning a perfect formulation score of 5 out of 5 stars, Creatine HMB also received high marks from our testing team for taste. Although it fell shy of another 5-star rating, this supplement earned a solid score of 4 out of 5 in this all-important category.

Recent findings suggest that transparent Labs Creatine HMB comes in 13 flavors, including an unflavored version. This is a lot more flavor options than you’ll find in most creatine supplements and the most of any on our list.

Recent findings suggest that pete Nastasi, C.P.T., C.S.N.C., tried this supplement. “I’ve tried both the Blue Raspberry and Strawberry Lemonade flavors, which are sweetened with stevia extract, and both tasted great,” he says. “I love having a flavored creatine supplement in the morning before my morning workout.”.

However, while Nastasi liked the flavor, other testers say this supplement has a slightly bitter taste, which they attribute to the BioPerine.

“I tried Black Cherry and I wasn’t a huge fan of the taste of this one—it tasted a bit watered down, even with the right amount of water,” our product tester noted. “Some people may prefer this though!”.

While another tester also noted some tartness due to the BioPerine, she’s still optimistic about the Tropical Punch flavor.

“I bought this at the end of winter but I’m looking forward to drinking it in the summer because I find something refreshing about it that I think will be nice during the hotter months,” she explained.

We chose Sports Research Creatine Monohydrate as our top pick for athletes because it contains 5 grams of creatine per serving, which research shows is an optimal dose for muscle gain, muscle recovery, and overall improved athletic performance. For this reason, we rated the formulation a 5 out of 5.

This creatine is also a great choice for athletes because it’s Informed Sport Certified—this third party tests for purity and banned substances. So, if you’re planning on competing in any events, you can feel good knowing this product is certified banned substance-free.

Another benefit of this supplement is that it uses micronized creatine. Micronized creatine is ground into finer particles than non-micronized so it dissolves much more easily in water. However, according to Nastasi, “micronized creatine is a bit of a marketing gimmick—it isn’t digested any better than standard creatine monohydrate.”.

Research supports Nastasi, as this 2022 study says there is “no evidence” that micronized creatine is more bioavailable than non-micronized creatine.

Sources indicate that however, using micronized creatine does contribute to excellent solubility. Our tester indicated no hesitation giving Sports Research Creatine Monohydrate a 5-star rating in this category.

“If you didn’t tell me there was creatine in this water I wouldn’t know—it’s truly tasteless and mixes easily,” our tester reported.

It has been revealed that unfortunately for your taste buds, this supplement only comes in an unflavored version. However, while some creatine powders can have a bitter aftertaste, this one doesn’t.

Sources indicate that “It tastes just like water,” our tester noted. One thing to consider about this creatine supplement is that it only comes as a powder. If you prefer creatine capsules (or a flavored powder), you’ll want to look elsewhere.

Industry observers note that if you don’t like measuring out and mixing powders, you’re in luck. Swoly Creatine Mono Gummies are ideal for athletes on the go who don’t want to carry around an additional shaker bottle for their creatine.

Although they only come in one flavor (Strawberry), Swoly knocked it out of the park from a taste perspective, earning a perfect score of 5 out of 5 from one of our most experienced product testers.

It has been revealed that “These are dangerously delicious — like, need-to-make-sure-my-child-doesn’t-find-these-or-she-will-eat-them all kind of delicious,” our tester eloquently described. “They remind me of the BEST fruit snacks.”.

Concerned about the texture? No need to worry about that, either. Our product tester also gave Swoly a 5-star rating for swallowability.

In a recent development, “Super easy and delicious. I’d eat these every day,” she noted.

As much as our tester enjoyed chowing down on these creatine gummies, be aware that one serving is five gummies, which can be a lot for some people. Plus, one serving only contains 4 grams of creatine monohydrate, which is a little shy of our preferred dosage of 5 grams. Our R.D. reviewer, Anna Marie Clear, notes that “larger individuals may need to take more of these gummies to get their research-backed dose of 0.1 grams of creatine per kilogram of body weight.”.

If that’s you, you may want to opt for a different option, since taking more than five gummies could “lead to GI symptoms because of the added sugar and gums,” she says.

In a recent development, unlike some other creatine supplements on this list, Swoly gummies contain more than a few added ingredients, including artificial ingredients. They also have 15 calories per serving and 2.5 grams of added sugar per serving from sucrose, dextrose, and maltodextrin.

As a result, we give the formulation 4 out of 5 stars since we prefer 5 grams of creatine monohydrate per serving and the added sugar may not align with some consumers’ dietary preferences.

In a recent development, although Swoly claims these gummies are third-party tested, there’s no information about through which organization. As a result, we could only give 3 out of 5 stars in this category.

If you’re looking for a budget-friendly creatine supplement, you can’t do much better than Nutricost. At just $0.20 per serving, this supplement is the cheapest on our list. But cheap doesn’t equate to low-quality—Nutricost creatine is third-party tested, which is something you typically only find in more expensive supplements.

According to recent reports, “This company does not elaborate on its third-party testing,” Clear indicates. “It’s hard to determine the brand’s safety without a detailed explanation of its testing process.”.

Although we docked a few points for the lack of transparency in third-party testing by giving 3 out of 5 stars, Nutricost earned a perfect formulation score.

“It’s recommended to take 3-5 grams of creatine daily to enhance athletic performance, and Nutricost provides 5 grams daily, ensuring your muscle cells remain saturated,” states registered dietitian Perry Nix.

In a recent development, our product tester reported no adverse side effects when taking Nutricost. In fact, he was pleasantly surprised that he didn’t experience any bloating like he did with other creatine products.

Recent findings suggest that another benefit of this creatine supplement is that it comes in five flavor options, which is more than most brands offer for creatine supplements. Flavors include Blue Raspberry, Fruit Punch, Pineapple Mango, Watermelon, and Unflavored. However, these flavors are sweetened with sucralose, which research shows may cause gut issues in some people when consumed in high doses.

According to recent reports, one of the few knocks against this budget-friendly creatine is its solubility; or potentially, the lack thereof. Our tester only gave it 3 out of 5 stars, noting that “it settles quite a bit.”.

Amazon reviewers are pleased with this product, giving it 4.6/5 stars overall. Many praise its lack of additional ingredients and effective formula. “It has made a significant positive impact on my workout performance and recovery,” indicates Amazon reviewer Kurt. However, a few reviewers mention finding pieces of plastic in their containers, which is something to watch out for.

Some unflavored creatine tastes chalky and a little bitter (no bueno!). If you drink your creatine with water, a flavored option like Legion Recharge should suit your taste buds better. Legion offers this supplement in six flavors, which although not as vast as Transparent Labs’ variety, taste better, according to customers and our team of experts.

Our product tester tried the Strawberry Lemonade flavor, giving it a perfect 5-out-of-5 rating for taste.

“It’s pretty sweet but also tart. I really liked it” she noted.

Many customers on Amazon attest to how good Legion’s flavors are, with a few noting that Strawberry Lemonade and Fruit Punch are particularly good. However, some reviewers mention the Unflavored version has an unpleasant, bitter flavor.

One thing you won’t have to worry about with Recharge is solubility. Our tester reported the power dissolved perfectly with no clumps or sediment at the bottom of her shaker cup, leading to another 5-out-of-5 rating.

It has been revealed that similarly, we’re also big fans of the formulation. Legion Recharge has a research-backed dose of 5g of creatine per serving. The creatine is micronized, which means it’s been processed to be finer. Legion claims this makes it easier to blend and less likely to cause an upset stomach. However, our R.D. reviewer Anna Marie Clear notes, “While micronized creatine monohydrate is processed to be finer, the research does not support the micronized version to be more bioavailable.”.

Legion Recharge also contains 2.1 grams of L-carnitine in each serving, which helps the body convert fat into energy, and 10.5 grams of corosolic acid, which research reveals helps regulate blood sugar.

Industry observers note that unfortunately for budget-conscious shoppers, Recharge is one of the more expensive options on this list, checking in at $1.33 per serving. As a result, we could only give it 1.5 out of 5 stars for price. So, if you’re on a tight budget, you may want to go with something like Nutricost.
